title: WPMS/1547/2015 of Yograj Vs Ram Kumar Gupta AND ANOTHER

paras.text:
WPMS No. 1547 of 2015
Hon'ble Alok Singh, J.
Mr. I.P. Kohli, Advocate for the
petitioner.
Application moved by the plaintiff -
petitioner, herein, under Section 21 (1) (a) of
the U.P. Act No. 13 of 1972 was dismissed
saying title of the landlord as well as
relationship of landlord and tenant has been
disputed by respondent no. 1, which cannot be
decided by the Prescribed Authority while
deciding application under Section 21 (1) (a) of
the U.P. Act No. 13 of 1972; appeal arising
therefrom was also dismissed. Feeling
aggrieved, plaintiff / petitioner, herein, has
preferred present writ petition under Article 227
of the Constitution of India.
Mr. I.P. Kohli, Advocate for the
petitioner fairly submits that Civil Suit for
cancellation of the sale deed in favour of the
petitioner, whereby petitioner derived title, is
pending disposal before the Civil Court. He
further submits that suit for cancellation of sale
deed was filed by respondent no. 1, herein.
Since title of the petitioner is in dispute,
which cannot be decided in proceedings under
Section 21 (1) (a) of the U.P. Act No. 13 of
1972, therefore, impugned judgment cannot be
faulted with. However, if so advised, petitioner
may file suit for possession in regular civil court
on the basis of title wherein if plaintiff /
petitioner, herein, is able to prove the title,
decree for possession can be passed against the
alleged tenant - respondent no. 1 on the ground
that he has wrongly denied the title of the
plaintiff - petitioner, herein.
In view of the above, I am not inclined to
entertain this writ petition. Writ petition is
dismissed in limine.
